Variable selection with unpenalized provider effects

Source: R/select_lasso.R
var_select.Rd

Lasso and group-lasso paths for the logistic model with fixed provider effects, \(\mathrm{logit}\, p_{ij} = \gamma_i + Z_{ij}^\top\beta\), where the provider effects (and any covariate named in penalize's complement) are never penalized. The objective at penalty \(\lambda\) is $$-\frac{1}{n}\,\ell(\gamma, \beta) + \lambda \sum_j m_j |\beta_j| \qquad \text{or} \qquad -\frac{1}{n}\,\ell(\gamma, \beta) + \lambda \sum_g m_g \|\beta_g\|_2,$$ solved by coordinate descent on standardized covariates (each penalized group orthonormalized) with one Newton step on the provider effects per cycle, warm starts along a decreasing sequence of \(\lambda\), and an active-set strategy.

Usage

var_select(
  data,
  penalty = c("lasso", "group_lasso"),
  group = NULL,
  penalize = NULL,
  multiplier = NULL,
  lambda = NULL,
  n_lambda = 100,
  lambda_min_ratio = 1e-04,
  standardize = TRUE,
  bound = 10,
  tol = 1e-04,
  max_iter = 10000,
  active_set = TRUE,
  mm = FALSE,
  backtrack = FALSE,
  threads = 1,
  model = NULL
)

Arguments

data

an object from pp_data() with a binary, binomial or survival outcome.

penalty

"lasso" (default) or "group_lasso".

group

for the group lasso, the group of each covariate: a vector of labels in the order of the covariates, or named by covariate. The label 0, NA or "" marks an unpenalized covariate.

penalize

names of the covariates that carry a penalty; default all. The others enter the model unpenalized.

multiplier

penalty multipliers \(m_j\) (named by covariate) or \(m_g\) (named by group); default 1 per covariate and the square root of the group size per group.

lambda

the penalty sequence; by default n_lambda values from the smallest \(\lambda\) with every penalized coefficient zero down to lambda_min_ratio times it, equally spaced on the log scale.

n_lambda, lambda_min_ratio

length and range of the default sequence.

standardize

centre and scale the covariates before penalizing (the estimates are returned on the original scale). Default TRUE.

bound

the provider effects are kept within median +/- bound.

tol

convergence tolerance on the largest change of a coefficient within a cycle. Default 1e-4.

max_iter

maximum number of cycles per value of lambda.

active_set

start each lambda from the coefficients that are nonzero and add the covariates that violate the optimality conditions.

mm

for the lasso, use the majorization with the constant working weight \(N/4\) instead of the IRLS weights (the group lasso always does). Default FALSE.

backtrack

line search in the provider-effect step. Default FALSE.

threads

OpenMP threads for the provider-effect step.

model

for a survival outcome: "cox" (default; the Cox model stratified by provider, whose baselines absorb the provider effects) or "discrete" (the discrete-time hazard model, lasso only). NULL for the other outcomes.

Value

An object of class pp_lasso (and pp_group_lasso for the group lasso):

beta

a matrix of covariate coefficients, one column per lambda.

gamma

a matrix of provider effects, one column per lambda (NULL for the stratified Cox model).

alpha, time_grid

the discrete-time model's period effects (one column per lambda) and the periods' times.

model

"logistic", "cox" or "discrete".

lambda, deviance, iter

per value of lambda (the deviance of the Cox model is minus twice its partial log-likelihood).

n_selected

number of penalized covariates with a nonzero coefficient per lambda.

penalized

logical, per covariate.

group

the group of each covariate (group lasso).

multiplier

the multipliers used.

data, vars, sizes, rows

as in fit_logistic_fe().

Details

Providers with fewer than the cutoff patients are excluded as in every fitter. The path starts from the fit with the unpenalized covariates only (or the provider-only model), whose residuals give the largest \(\lambda\). The deviance reported per \(\lambda\) is \(-2\ell\) without the constant term.

With a survival outcome (pp_data() with time and event) the paths are those of grplasso's Strat.cox() and pp.DiscSurv():

  • model = "cox": the weighted partial likelihood of the Cox model with one baseline per provider, counting-process rows (start, stop], case weights and offsets as in fit_cox(); the provider effects are not parameters (gamma is NULL) and the working weight is 1 (Breheny and Huang's majorization for the Cox model). The covariates of a group are orthonormalized as for the logistic model.

  • model = "discrete": \(\mathrm{logit}\, h_{jk} = \alpha_k + \gamma_i + Z_j^\top\beta\) for subject \(j\) of provider \(i\) in period \(k\), the periods being the distinct values of time; one row per subject (no start, no weights), the subject at risk in every period up to its own. The period effects \(\alpha\) and the provider effects \(\gamma\) are unpenalized, \(\gamma\) identified by a zero median (grplasso fixed the first provider at zero) and kept within +/- bound; the likelihood is computed without expanding the data. The IRLS weights \(\sum_k h_{jk}(1 - h_{jk})\) or, with mm = TRUE, \(t_j / 4\).

References

Breheny P, Huang J (2015). Group descent algorithms for nonconvex penalized linear and logistic regression models with grouped predictors. Statistics and Computing, 25, 173-187.

Yang Y, Wu W, He K (2025+). Variable selection for provider profiling with high-dimensional fixed effects (the grplasso package).

See also

cv(), coef.pp_lasso(), predict.pp_lasso()

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, n_covariates = 6, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = paste0("x", 1:6), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
path <- var_select(pd, n_lambda = 20)
path
#> Lasso path of the logistic model with unpenalized provider effects
#>   2679 rows, 20 providers, 6 covariates (6 penalized)
#>   20 values of lambda from 0.09666 to 9.666e-06; selected covariates from 0 to 6
coef(path, lambda = path$lambda[10])$beta
#>         x1         x2         x3         x4         x5         x6 
#>  0.5670012 -0.3142008  0.2640520  0.5155683 -0.3474599  0.2350394 
grp <- var_select(pd, penalty = "group_lasso", group = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 0), n_lambda = 20)
